scope: phase_D_brief_reader; supplied full current source/tests and explicitly labeled integration diff if present

findings.title: Brief collection errors leave an unused reservation committed
findings.issue: The bare `except Exception` around `execute_reserved` swallows collector failures after `authorize_and_reserve`, and no `abandon_before_transport` runs for the failed reservation. Unlike the editorial path's `finally`, a failed source collection can leave the reservation reserved/committed, consuming budget for work that never produced evidence.
findings.fix: Ensure every reserved decision is either settled after a successful transport or abandoned in an exception path (e.g. `finally`/except calling `abandon_before_transport`) before marking the source unavailable.

findings.title: Reader artifact cache key ignores version, breaking immutable version isolation
findings.issue: The artifact path key hashes only `owner_ref + content_digest + format`, not `brief_id`/`version`. A bound document's rendered body is cached and reused across requests by content digest; if the same content digest is ever re-bound under a different version or the DB row is superseded while the file remains, the pre-render/post-render existence and index checks can serve or resurrect content outside the requested immutable version lineage.
findings.fix: Include `brief_id` and `version` in the artifact key (or key strictly by the manifest storage digest including version) so each immutable version has its own isolated artifact and deletion/index state.

not_verified: Modules outside the supplied phase-D scope were not reviewed; the integration diff is context only and unchanged legacy code was not verified.
Behavior of `prm.storage.policy`, `execute_reserved`, `ScopedModelClient`, and registry settle semantics was inferred from call sites, not reviewed source.
No live runs were performed; only static review of supplied source/tests and hashes.
Subprocess render dependencies (WeasyPrint/report_exports) internals and network_guard bypass via C-level sockets were not fully verified.
findings.summary: The reviewed phase-D modules are broadly careful: owner/scope checks, bounded hooks and batches, format/allowlist enforcement, digests for immutable Brief versions, isolated rendering with network block and resource limits, and deletion-aware artifact indexing are present. Two reproducible medium-confidence P1s stand out: a swallowed collector exception can leak an un-abandoned reservation (contrary to the clean editorial `finally` pattern), and the report cache key omits brief_id/version despite serving version-addressed immutable documents. No P0 was found in the supplied scope; fix the P1s before shipping.
